theses.theme: Oil-driven inflation forces the Fed to hike: sustained high crude favors oilfield services and midstream over the integrated majors
theses.causal_chain: Spiraling oil prices feed headline inflation -> the Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, and signaled another this year -> if crude stays elevated and policy stays restrictive, producers keep capital discipline and spend on maintenance, well-service intensity and takeaway capacity rather than buybacks alone -> revenue shifts toward oilfield service, equipment and pipeline/midstream firms, which are priced for much lower activity than the integrated majors.
theses.second_order: Oilfield services, drilling and completion equipment makers, pipeline and midstream operators, and industrial suppliers to energy capex. They benefit from sustained activity and volume, not just the spot crude price.
theses.invalidation_condition: Brent crude closes more than 15% below its 2026-10-02 close for 10 consecutive trading days, or the Fed signals it will not hike again and begins guiding toward cuts, before the horizon date.

theses.theme: Higher-for-longer policy rates: asset-sensitive regional and mid-cap banks and non-bank lenders over the money-center banks
theses.causal_chain: The Fed hiked to 3.75%-4% and projections point to another increase this year, with AI-related investment cited as a possible inflationary factor -> the front end of the curve reprices upward and the 'transitory' narrative is discredited -> banks with floating-rate loan books, cheap core deposits and short-duration securities see net interest income expand -> earnings estimates for these banks lag, while the large money-center banks already trade as consensus beneficiaries of rates and capital markets.
theses.second_order: Regional and community banks with asset-sensitive balance sheets, floating-rate lenders and short-duration credit managers. They benefit from wider loan yields and from deposit costs that lag policy rates.
theses.invalidation_condition: The Fed cuts rates or officially signals an end to hikes before the horizon date, or the 2s10s Treasury curve inverts by more than 50bp, or the KBW Regional Banking Index underperforms the S&P 500 by more than 10 percentage points between 2026-10-03 and the horizon.

theses.theme: AI/capex-driven demand keeps inflation sticky, so grid equipment makers and merchant power generators benefit more than the AI chip and hyperscaler leaders
theses.causal_chain: The FOMC raised the funds rate to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and its statement describes capital investment as robust and productivity growth as strong. CNBC reports economists see expanded AI investment as a potential inflationary factor. If the Fed keeps tightening while AI and datacenter capex stays strong, the spending is physically constrained by electricity, transformers, switchgear and generation capacity. Those bottleneck suppliers can raise prices and lengthen backlogs, and they are less exposed than the chip and hyperscaler leaders if capex multiples compress under higher discount rates. Contracted or merchant power and electrical equipment earn pricing power from scarcity, not from cheap financing.
theses.second_order: Electrical and grid equipment manufacturers (transformers, switchgear, cooling and power distribution) and merchant or independent power generators with datacenter offtake. These sit one step behind the AI leaders and are still priced largely as cyclicals or regulated yield proxies.
theses.invalidation_condition: Thesis is invalid if, before the horizon date, two or more of the top hyperscalers cut their forward capex guidance, or the Fed reverses and cuts the funds rate below 3.75%. It is also invalid if the S&P 500 Industrials sector underperforms the S&P 500 by more than 8 percentage points over the period.

theses.theme: Robust capex plus sticky 3.4% inflation supports the electrification metals supply chain (copper and electrical inputs) as an underpriced input to the investment cycle
theses.causal_chain: BLS data cited by Citizens Bank show consumer prices up 3.4% year over year through July 2026, and the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 while calling capital investment robust and activity solid. Strong capex in power, grid and datacenter build-outs consumes physical inputs such as copper and electrical steel. Inflation that stays above target, with a Fed that has to keep raising rates, tends to keep nominal commodity demand and pricing resilient where the demand is investment-driven rather than rate-sensitive housing. Miners and materials producers tied to electrification are therefore a second-order claim on the same capex wave. The market prices them mostly on China cyclicality, not on this US capex demand.
theses.second_order: Copper miners, aluminum and electrical-steel producers, and wire and cable suppliers. These supply the build-out and are not the AI leaders themselves.
theses.invalidation_condition: Thesis is invalid if front-month COMEX copper falls more than 15% from its level at 2026-10-10 and holds below that level for 30 consecutive days before the horizon date. It is also invalid if year-over-year CPI falls below 2.5% in two consecutive prints, which would remove the sticky-inflation leg.

theses.theme: US gas-oil price dislocation: LNG export growth and unhedged gas producers over the integrated majors
theses.causal_chain: Brent settled at $109.86 on 16 Oct, its highest since May, on Middle East and Russian supply disruptions. Henry Hub gas was only about $3.12/MMBtu, so US gas trades at a deep discount to the global energy complex. US LNG plants shipped 35 cargoes in the week to 14 Oct, and FERC is proposing blanket authorizations to speed up LNG project permitting. High oil and import-security concerns keep overseas buyers looking for non-Gulf LNG, which pulls more US feedgas demand. That tightens the domestic gas balance while spot gas is still cheap. Gas-weighted producers and LNG export or feedgas infrastructure capture the rerating. The integrated majors are already priced for $110 oil.
theses.second_order: Gas-weighted E&Ps with unhedged volumes, LNG feedgas pipelines and LNG exporters with merchant volumes. Gas-fired generators also gain as US gas-to-power and export demand grows. This is a gas-versus-oil spread trade. It is not the oil-services or midstream-on-crude trade.
theses.invalidation_condition: Henry Hub front-month settles below $2.50/MMBtu for 10 consecutive trading days, or EIA-reported weekly US LNG cargoes average below 30 over any 8-week stretch, before the horizon date.

theses.theme: Munitions and missile-defense replenishment: the defense supply chain over the prime contractors
theses.causal_chain: Congress lifted FY2026 US national defense discretionary spending more than 17% to about $1.05 trillion. Missile and drone strikes on energy infrastructure are now driving oil, including a Yanbu missile strike that helped push Brent to $110. Sustained use of air defense and long-range munitions, together with record budgets, creates a multi-year replenishment and capacity-expansion cycle. The prime contractors are the consensus winners. Bottlenecks and margin upside sit with sub-tier suppliers: energetics and propellants, solid rocket motors, castings and forgings, precision components and defense electronics. They have less index visibility and lower valuation premiums.
theses.second_order: Sub-tier and mid-cap defense suppliers (energetics, rocket motors, forgings, RF and electronic components) and specialty metals inputs. These firms get volume and pricing from prime-contractor capacity ramps.
theses.invalidation_condition: A negotiated de-escalation that takes Brent below $90 and holds it there for 30 days, or an enacted FY2027 defense appropriation or continuing resolution that cuts procurement and munitions accounts below FY2026 enacted levels, before the horizon date.

theses.theme: Real-wage squeeze and stagnating payrolls drive trade-down: discount, dollar-channel and off-price retail over the big-box leaders
theses.causal_chain: September CPI rose 3.7% year over year and PPI rose 6.3%. Wage growth has slowed to about 3.0–3.1%, so real wages are falling. September payrolls rose only 29,000 against an 84,000 forecast, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. The 30-year mortgage rate is 7.40% and the 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.1–5.2%, which limits household credit capacity. Lower- and middle-income households facing negative real wage growth shift spending to dollar stores, off-price and value formats. These channels are less crowded than the mega-cap retail leaders and benefit from vendor-sourced closeout inventory when brands over-order.
theses.second_order: Dollar-channel and off-price retailers and value-oriented packaged goods and private-label suppliers. These are the beneficiaries of trade-down behavior, as opposed to the large-cap retail and staples leaders.
theses.invalidation_condition: Year-over-year growth in average hourly earnings re-accelerates above CPI inflation for two consecutive monthly reports, or the dollar-channel and off-price retailer group posts negative comparable-store sales in its next two quarterly reports, before the horizon date.

theses.theme: Producer-price pass-through: PPI running well ahead of CPI favors pricing-power industrial distributors over the industrial conglomerate leaders
theses.causal_chain: September PPI rose 6.3% y/y against CPI of 3.7%, which means input-cost inflation is running well ahead of what has reached consumers (CNBC, 16 Oct 2026). The Fed under Warsh is treating the inflation as a problem and has already hiked, with another hike priced for December. Industrial MRO and electrical distributors reprice from list prices and supplier price increases quickly, and their inventory is marked up as costs rise. Their gross margins have typically held or widened in the early-to-mid stage of producer-price inflation, in the way they did in 2021-22. Manufacturers and capital-goods leaders carry fixed-price backlogs and tariff and input-cost lag, so they are more likely to see margin compression. The distribution layer is therefore a cheaper, less crowded way to own the industrial inflation pass-through.
theses.second_order: Broadline MRO, electrical and fastener distributors (GWW, FAST, WCC, POOL-type channel businesses) capture list-price inflation with little capital intensity. Their revenue is tied to the existing installed base and maintenance spend rather than new-build orders. The effect should show up as gross-margin and price/cost spread beats in Q3 and Q4 2026 earnings.
theses.invalidation_condition: Headline PPI final-demand y/y falls below 4.0% in any monthly release before the horizon, or the leading distributors report gross margin contracting y/y for two consecutive quarters (a sign that price/cost has turned negative).
